label: TMUA 2022 · Paper 1 · Question 9

hints.title: Eliminate one of the functions
hints.body: Use the difference equation to express g(x) in terms of f(x) and sinx. Substitute that expression into the product equation.
hints.recap: Two equations involving two function values can be handled as simultaneous algebraic equations at each input.
hints.pitfall: Both equations must be used at the same value of the input.
hints.pause: Obtain a quadratic equation in the value of the first function.

recall.reminder: Expressing one unknown in terms of another allows substitution into a second equation.

hints.title: Complete a square using the trig identity
hints.body: Your quadratic contains f(x)2−2f(x)sinx. Complete this to a square, then simplify with sin2x+cos2x=1.
hints.recap: The trigonometric identity removes the remaining input-dependent term from the squared equation.
hints.pitfall: Taking a square root introduces both possible signs.
hints.pause: Write the possible function values at a given input.

recall.reminder: The identity between sine squared and cosine squared often turns mixed trigonometric expressions into a constant.

hints.title: Find a bound and check that it is achievable
hints.body: Apply −1≤sinx≤1 to each branch. A proposed least value must both bound every permitted value and occur for functions satisfying the original equations.
hints.recap: An attainable lower bound gives the requested minimum.
hints.pitfall: Do not discard one square-root branch or assume the same branch must be chosen at every input.
hints.pause: Find the least value across the branches, then exhibit a valid function pair and an input attaining it.

recall.reminder: Find the range of the inner expression before optimising an expression built from it.

solution:
Write g(x)=f(x)−2sinx. Substitution into the product gives f(x)2−2f(x)sinx−cos2x=0. Completing the square and using sin2x+cos2x=1 yields (f(x)−sinx)2=1.

Thus at every input, f(x)=sinx+1 or f(x)=sinx−1. Because −1≤sinx≤1, every permitted value of f(x) is at least −2.

The choice f(x)=sinx−1, g(x)=−sinx−1 satisfies both original equations for every real input, and has value −2 when x=3π/2. The lower bound is therefore attained. Answer E.
knowledgePattern: Eliminate one function, expose pointwise branches and use the sine range
